content:
Irene: Quick follow-up from the residency RFC. Instead of full active/active consensus, I sketched a regional-escrow + consent-token flow that trades strict sync for predictable local-failover. Quick reactions?

Sam: Interesting. What does escrow represent here? A lease pointer to the owner region?

Irene: Yes. Escrow is an ownership pointer (tenant -> region). Proxies query escrow in a fast KV. If local==owner -> local writes. If not -> three options: sync-forward, queue-for-fanout, or serve read-only, chosen by tenant policy.

Nate: Sync-forward will still pay cross-region latency. How do we avoid spiking p95?

Maya: Add a short-lived consent token cached at proxies. Format like `consent:v2:<tenant>:<epoch>:<region>`. If token present we fast-path to owner with fewer checks. If absent, fallback to conservative path. TTL maybe 15s-2m.

Irene: Also support optimistic local-write for low-risk tenants: write provisional record locally, return success to client, then a reconciliation job posts to owner for finalization. Use fencing IDs to prevent double-apply.

Sam: Provisional writes and PII are a red flag. We need per-tenant allowedModes = [owner-only, eventual, read-only]. Control-plane should store this and proxies should enforce.

Nate: How do we withdraw consent fast when policy changes or ownership flips?

Maya: Control-plane increments an epoch counter for the tenant. Consent tokens include epoch. Proxies compare token epoch with manifest epoch; mismatch invalidates token immediately. We'll also expose a revocation fanout to edge proxies for quick eviction.

Irene: Good. DB invariants? We'll require owner region to mint global monotonic ids or sequence stamps. Provisional records get local provisional-id and later get correlated to owner-id during reconcile. If conflict, reconciliation emits compensating ops.

Sam: We should specify headers for forwarded calls so owner can audit and see decision context. Suggest `X-RW-Residency: owner=us-west;consent=consent:v2:...;policy=eventual`.

Nate: Telemetry: mark every request with `residency.path` = {local-owner, forwarded, queued, rejected}. Also collect `residency.latency_ms` and `residency.reconcile_lag_ms`. Need tenant-tagged metrics for rollouts.

Irene: Ops automation: add a reconciliation worker that processes provisional queues, applies id-mapping, and emits compensating deletes on conflicts. Worker should be horizontally scalable and idempotent.

Maya: Security/compliance: when tenant has PII_flag, escrow values must be stored encrypted (KMS) and cross-region forwards must emit audit events and be logged to the tenant's audit sink.

Sam: Can we see a short pseudo-flow for the proxy? Want to confirm timeouts and fallbacks.

Irene: Pseudo: 
```
# proxy flow
manifest = getTenantManifest(tenant)
if escrow.owner == local {
  writeLocal()
  emit(metric:residency.path=local-owner)
  return 200
}
if manifest.allowed == "read-only" {
  return 403
}
if cachedConsent.valid() && manifest.allowed == "sync" {
  resp = forwardToOwner(timeout=250ms)
  if resp.ok return 200
  else if manifest.allow_eventual {
    enqueueProvisional()
    return 202
  } else return 504
}
# fallback
if manifest.allowed == "eventual" {
  enqueueProvisional()
  return 202
}
return 409
```

Nate: Timeout numbers look reasonable. We should gate those with per-tenant SLO overrides for latency-sensitive customers.

Maya: For rollout: canary on low-risk tenants in a single region pair. Measure forwarded-p95, provisional reconciliation lag, and conflict rate. Ops-bot can synth-run for 24h before widening.

ops-bot: quick sim uploaded -> https://ci.redwood/sims/escrow-consent/3665432100 with p95 breakdowns. With 70% cached-consent hits simulated, forwarded p95 drops ~40% at application level.

Irene: Implementation owners I propose: escrow KV + token epoching (Maya / eng-runtime), proxy decision + headers (Sam / eng-platform), manifest store + revocation fanout (product/infra), reconciliation worker (Nate / eng-sre).

Sam: I'll take proxy changes.

Nate: I'll take the reconciliation worker.

Maya: I'll own escrow KV and token lifecycle.

Irene: I'll draft a short RFC addendum with sequence diagrams, proto header spec, and the canary gating plan. Thanks all. :rocket:

deploy-bot: artifacts and sim logs uploaded -> https://ci.redwood/sims/escrow-consent/3665432100
